component.name: iPhone
component.summary: Your iPhone's messages, notifications, and calls on the Linux desktop

description.p: The iPhone app, from the iphonebridge project, brings a paired iPhone to the Linux desktop over standard Bluetooth profiles — no Mac relay, no cloud service, no subscription.
This app is the graphical front-end for the iphonebridge daemon:

ul.li: Read SMS and iMessage conversations and send replies
A live feed of every app's notifications, mirrored over ANCS
Take and place phone calls — caller ID, answer, decline, dial
Control what the iPhone is playing — music, podcasts, audiobooks — with cover art, transport and volume
Daemon health and first-run setup guidance

screenshot.caption: Conversations, with the state of the Bluetooth link
Place a call, answer or hang up an active one
Every app's notifications, mirrored over ANCS
Service health, the iPhone toggles, and what is stored here

description.p: Notifications from iPhone apps come back by themselves after a reboot. Desktop popups work even when the notification server starts after the iPhone app, and the Status tab no longer reports notifications as working when they are not.
Calls come back by themselves after the oFono telephony service restarts or crashes; the daemon no longer needs a restart.
Messages and contacts come up sooner after the iPhone's toggles are turned on, and the daemon reports whether calls and media control work, so setup can wait until everything does.

The per-app notifications setup no longer breaks calls on BlueZ 5.86 and later: it keeps BlueZ's own Hands-Free client off, which competed with oFono for the iPhone. The install steps start the pairing on the iPhone.
The app is named iPhone in the app launcher, the window title, the app name on desktop notifications and the software-centre listing.
Per-app notifications, media controls and the battery level work for an iPhone that BlueZ first saw over Bluetooth LE, which the daemon could not find before.

The daemon runs confined by an AppArmor profile and no longer uses sudo: a polkit rule lets it start the one system unit that sets the Bluetooth adapter's class, and the package no longer creates a group or installs sudoers rules. Cover art shows again while BlueZ's mpris-proxy holds the iPhone's image channel.

A Clear all button at the foot of the Notifications tab dismisses every notification at once, on the phone too where it still can. The dismiss button on a notification card no longer sits under the scrollbar on KDE. The daemon no longer shows every notification many times over after Bluetooth reconnections, and on startup it removes the copies an earlier version already logged.

The doctor command no longer reports per-app notifications available while the phone is connected over classic Bluetooth only, a state the app's Status tab already reported as Not detected. The documentation now describes the ANCS grant as iOS offers it: a third Bluetooth toggle, Share System Notifications.

Messages from different shortcodes no longer share one conversation. A five- or six-digit sender, such as a transit or bank alert, was too short to be read as a number, so every one of them fell back to the same thread.

The Music tab is now Now Playing: it controls podcasts and audiobooks exactly as it controls music. The emoji picker shows each emoji once rather than once per spelling, and names the one under the cursor. The window opens taller so the Status page fits.
The emoji picker offers skin tones, chosen from the button beside its search field and remembered between sessions.
An emoji picker in the composer with search and a recently-used tab, emoji drawn larger than the words in messages, and a fix for uneven text on fractional-scale displays.
The Status tab now shows the phone's vitals: battery, cellular carrier and signal bars, and the model by its marketing name. A desktop notification warns when the phone's battery runs low.
New Music tab: control the iPhone's playback while its audio plays through this computer — album art, play/pause, skip, volume, and shuffle/repeat.

Notifications can be dismissed from either end: dismissing a card in the app clears the notification on the iPhone, and clearing it on the iPhone removes the card from the app. The status page no longer reports app notifications as working while the phone is disconnected.
The man pages now report the correct version.

Per-app notifications are now attainable: the setup command steers the connection over BLE and iOS asks for permission on the phone. The doctor command checks BLE advertising and the ANCS bond, and man pages are included.
The interface is styled after Apple's and follows the desktop's font size. Emoji are legible, the Setup tab is now Status, and starting a new conversation no longer leaves the previous one on screen.
The desktop app is rebuilt on Qt 6 / QML. Message and app notifications now clear themselves after ten seconds, and a conversation with your own number no longer splits in two.
Fixes repeated confirmation codes being dropped, duplicated and truncated messages, and verification codes reaching the journal.
Read-state syncs both ways, timestamps are stored in UTC, and the interface was restyled.
First desktop app — conversations, a notification feed, call UI, and a setup/status page.
